terms.usage: Everyday word for father, to address him and to talk about him (CC-CEDICT '(coll.) father'; HSK 1). In HSK samples children address their fathers as 爸爸 or the short 爸 ('爸，您为什么要问我这么简单的问题？'). For your partner's father: normally from the wedding on (改口), earlier only if the parents invite it; before that he is 叔叔 or 伯父.
terms.speaker: either
terms.regional_note: relationship.js lists many colloquial/regional alternatives (e.g. 老爸, 爹, 阿爸, 老汉) without regions — note that in standard Mandarin 老汉 means 'old man' (现代汉语词典); its Guangdong locale gives the Cantonese 老窦. Xinhua: 大大 is a dialect word for father ('方言。称父亲'); CC-CEDICT: '(dialect) dad / uncle'.

terms.usage: Address and everyday reference (CC-CEDICT '(coll.) paternal grandfather; grandpa'; HSK 2). Formal/written equivalent: 祖父. Also a respectful title for any old man, usually with the surname (HSK 2025 syllabus: 张爷爷; Xinhua sense 3 '对男性尊长的称呼').
terms.speaker: either
terms.regional_note: relationship.js's Guangdong locale gives the Cantonese 阿爷; its main list also has 阿公, 嗲嗲, 爹爹 and others (regions not stated). terms.usage: Everyday word for mother, to address her and to talk about her (CC-CEDICT 'mama; mommy; mother'; HSK 1). Children address her as 妈妈 or the short 妈 (HSK samples: '妈妈，谢谢您！', '妈，您的手机响了。'). For your partner's mother: normally from the wedding on (改口), earlier only if the parents invite it; before that she is 阿姨 or 伯母. 你妈 is fine inside a sentence (Tatoeba: '你和你妈用上海话聊天的时候…'), but as a bare exclamation it is a curse (CC-CEDICT), so 你妈妈 sounds gentler when you speak of your partner's mother.
terms.speaker: either
terms.regional_note: 姆妈 is a dialect word for mum (CC-CEDICT '(dialect) mom; mother'; 现代汉语词典 〈方〉 ❶母亲); relationship.js lists further variants (阿妈, 老妈, 娘, 姆妈 …) without regions; its Guangdong locale gives the Cantonese 老母.

terms.usage: HSK 2025: xífu (level 6). The two senses differ in pronunciation: CC-CEDICT xífu '(dialect) wife; (dialect) young married woman' vs xífù 'daughter-in-law; wife of a younger brother or relative of the younger generation'; 现代汉语词典 likewise has 媳妇 xífù (son's wife; wife of a younger relative: 侄媳妇, 孙媳妇) and 媳妇儿 xí·fur 〈方〉 (wife; young married woman). verification.notes: Correction: the old English '(north, colloquial) wife; also daughter-in-law' put both senses under the one pinyin xífu, but the 'daughter-in-law' sense is read xífù (CC-CEDICT 媳妇 xi2 fu4; 现代汉语词典 媳妇 xífù ❶儿子的妻子 ❷晚辈亲属的妻子), while 'wife' is the regional 媳妇(儿) xífu(r) (CC-CEDICT xi2 fu5 '(dialect) wife'; 现代汉语词典 媳妇儿 xí·fur 〈方〉 ❶妻子). English and usage now separate them; pinyin xífu kept (HSK 2025; 'wife' sense). address_form false kept as a conservative inference (northern husbands may also call their wife 媳妇儿 directly — not sourced here). Checker: OK. Previous values: english = "(north, colloquial) wife; also daughter-in-law"; usage = "HSK 2025: xífu (level 6). Xinhua: ① '儿子的妻子' (son's wife; also wives of younger relatives: 弟媳妇, 侄媳妇); ② '方言。北方称妻子' (dialect: in the north, 'wife'). CC-CEDICT splits the readings: xífù 'daughter-in-law; wife of a younger brother or relative of the younger generation', xífu '(dialect) wife; (dialect) young married woman'.".

rules.rule: Several relatives of the same kind are numbered by birth order (排行): 大 for the eldest (大伯, 大姑, 大舅, 大姨), then 二, 三, 四… (二叔, 三姨), and 小 for the youngest (小姑, 小姨). Some regions use other words for 'youngest', which relationship.js treats as equal to 小 (e.g. 幺, 细, 满, 尾).
rules.why: Xinhua 排行: '兄弟姐妹依长幼排列的次序'. CC-CEDICT: 大伯 'father's older brother (esp. his oldest brother)', 大姑 'father's oldest sister', 小姑 'father's youngest sister', 大姨 'mother's eldest sister', 小姨 'mother's youngest sister', 老幺 '(coll.) youngest child'. relationship.js numbers relatives 大 = 1, 二, 三 … and 小 = last, and rewrites the prefixes 尕, 幺, 细, 满, 碎, 晚, 末, 尾, 幼 to 小.
rules.regional_note: relationship.js does not say which 'youngest' prefix belongs to which region.

rules.rule: Most relatives have an everyday term, often doubled (爷爷, 伯伯, 叔叔, 姑姑), and a formal/written one (祖父, 叔父, 姑母); you call people by the everyday term. 伯父/伯母 are the exception that also serve as respectful titles.
rules.why: Xinhua: 外祖父 '母亲的父亲。俗称外公' (commonly called 外公), 外祖母 '…俗称外婆'. CC-CEDICT marks everyday forms as colloquial — 爷爷 '(coll.) paternal grandfather; grandpa', 姑妈 '(coll.)', 婶子 '(coll.)' — and calls 伯父 a 'term of respect' and 伯母 a 'polite form of address'. HSK 2025 puts 爷爷/奶奶 at level 2 but 祖父/祖母 at level 7-9.

rules.rule: 外 ('outside') marks relatives through a woman: 外公/外婆 (mother's parents), 外孙/外孙女 (daughter's children), 外甥/外甥女 (sister's children). The counterparts through a man have no 外: 爷爷/奶奶, 孙子/孙女, 侄子/侄女.
rules.why: CC-CEDICT: 外孙 'daughter's son; grandson; descendant via the female line'; 外公 'mother's father'; 外甥 'sister's son'; 侄子 'brother's son; nephew'; 孙子 'grandson; son's son'. Xinhua: 外祖父 '母亲的父亲'.

rules.rule: For the mother's parents there are two pairs: 外公/外婆 and 姥爷/姥姥. Both are taught (HSK 2025, level 5) and understood everywhere. 姥爷/姥姥 is the northern pair and the one the 现代汉语词典 treats as standard, labelling 外公/外婆 〈方〉; but 外公/外婆 is the everyday pair in the south — when a Shanghai textbook replaced 外婆 with 姥姥 in 2018, it caused a public outcry. For a family from south/central China expect 外公/外婆 (or a local word) — check with your partner.
rules.why: relationship.js main list 'm,f':['外公',…,'姥爷',…], 'm,m':['外婆',…,'姥姥',…]; 北方 locale 'm,f':['姥爷'], 'm,m':['姥姥']; readme example setMode('northern', {'m,f':['姥爷'], 'm,m':['姥姥'], …}). HSK 2025: 外公 wàigōng, 外婆 wàipó, 姥爷 lǎoye, 姥姥 lǎolao, all level 5.
rules.regional_note: North: 姥爷/姥姥; south: 外公/外婆; Cantonese: 阿公/阿婆 (relationship.js locales; 现代汉语词典 labels; 2018 Shanghai textbook controversy).

sources.publisher: 中国新闻网 (China News Service)
sources.evidence: Search-result summary returned by WebSearch; the page itself could not be opened from the sandbox. In June 2018 a Shanghai second-grade Chinese textbook (上海教育出版社) changed 外婆 to 姥姥 in the lesson 《打碗碗花》; a circulated education-commission reply called 外婆 a dialect word; the change drew wide public objection, and the author 李天芳 said both words are understood in north and south. verification.notes: Correction: the old rule called both pairs 'standard Mandarin'. 现代汉语词典 labels 外公/外婆 〈方〉 and gives 姥爷/姥姥 unlabelled — the point at the centre of the 2018 Shanghai textbook controversy, when 外婆 was replaced by 姥姥 and the public objected (chinanews.com, Language Log via search). Both pairs are in HSK 2025 (level 5) and understood everywhere; for a family from south/central China 外公/外婆 is the expected pair. The rule now says this. Previous values: rule = "For the mother's parents, relationship.js uses 外公/外婆 by default and 姥爷/姥姥 in its northern (北方) locale; both pairs are standard Mandarin (both in HSK 2025, level 5). For a family from south/central China the northern pair is the less likely one, but local words also exist — check with your partner."; regional_note = "North: 姥爷/姥姥; default elsewhere: 外公/外婆; Guangdong locale: 阿公/阿婆 (all per relationship.js).".

rules.rule: Your mother's brothers are all 舅舅 (numbered 大舅, 二舅…, 小舅) whatever their age relative to her; her sisters are 姨/姨妈 (大姨, 二姨…, 小姨). Their spouses are 舅妈 and 姨父.

rules.rule: Cousins are 堂 or 表. 堂 cousins are your father's brothers' children (the paternal line, same clan); 表 cousins are the children of your father's sisters, your mother's brothers and your mother's sisters. Then add 哥/姐/弟/妹 by sex and by age relative to you: 堂哥, 表妹…
rules.why: CC-CEDICT: 堂 'relationship between cousins etc on the paternal side of a family / of the same clan'; 表 'family relationship via females'; 堂哥 'older male patrilineal cousin'; 表哥 'older male cousin through a female relative'. Xinhua 表兄: '姑母、舅父、姨母之子，年长于己者称表兄'; 姑表 vs 姨表 name the two kinds of 表 link. relationship.js prefixes: 'f,xb' 堂, 'f,xs' 姑表, 'm,xb' 舅表, 'm,xs' 姨表.

sources.title: 《现代汉语词典》（第7版）全文TXT, entry 【堂】
sources.publisher: 中国社会科学院语言研究所词典编辑室 / 商务印书馆 (The Commercial Press); community transcription github.com/CNMan/XDHYCD7th (5th-edition text being updated to the 7th edition; senses after the letter a not yet fully revised)
sources.evidence: 【堂】tánɡ❶正房：～屋。❷专为某种活动用的房屋：礼～｜课～｜食～。❸〈名〉旧时官府中举行仪式、审讯案件的地方：大～｜过～。❹用于厅堂名称，旧时也指某一家、某一房或某一家族：三槐～。❺用于商店牌号：同仁～（北京的一家药店）。❻堂房：～兄｜～弟｜～姊妹。❼〈量〉a）用于成套的家具：一～家具。b）用于分节的课程，一节叫一堂：两～课。c）旧时审案一次叫一堂：过了两～。d）用于场景、壁画等：三～内景｜一～壁画。❽（Tánɡ）〈名〉姓。 (line 50497)

sources.title: 《现代汉语词典》（第7版）全文TXT, entry 【表】
sources.publisher: 中国社会科学院语言研究所词典编辑室 / 商务印书馆 (The Commercial Press); community transcription github.com/CNMan/XDHYCD7th (5th-edition text being updated to the 7th edition; senses after the letter a not yet fully revised)
sources.evidence: 【表】（⓫錶）biāo❶外面；外表：～面｜地～｜由～及里。❷中表（亲戚）：～哥｜～叔｜姨～｜姑～。❸〈动〉把思想感情显示出来；表示：～达｜～态｜～决心｜深～同情｜按下不～（说）。❹〈动〉俗称用药物把感受的风寒发散出来：吃服（fù）药～一～，出身汗，病就好了。❺榜样；模范：～率｜为人师～。❻古代文体奏章的一种，用于较重大的事件：诸葛亮《出师～》。❼〈名〉用表格形式排列事项的书籍或文件：《史记》十～｜统计～｜一张～。❽刻有文字或图案的石柱或石碑：华～｜墓～。❾古代测日影的标杆。参看490页【圭表】。❿〈名〉测量某种量（liànɡ）的器具：温度～｜电～｜水～｜煤气～。⓫〈名〉计时的器具，一般指比钟小而可以随身携带的：怀～｜手～｜秒～｜电子～｜买了一块～。⓬（Biǎo）〈名〉姓。 (line 3334)

rules.rule: Older siblings are addressed by their title — 哥/哥哥, 姐/姐姐, or numbered (大哥, 二哥) — as in the HSK samples.

rules.rule: Husband/wife words differ in register: 老公/老婆 are colloquial; 丈夫/妻子 are the standard words; 爱人 means 'spouse' in mainland China (but 'lover' elsewhere); 先生/太太 also mean husband/wife.
rules.why: CC-CEDICT: 老公 '(coll.) husband', 老婆 '(coll.) wife', 丈夫 'husband', 妻子 'wife', 爱人 'spouse (PRC); lover (non-PRC)', 先生 '… husband', 太太 '… wife'. HSK 2025: 丈夫/妻子 level 2, 爱人 level 3, 老公/老婆 level 5.

rules.rule: In-law words depend on whose family it is: a wife's in-laws are 公公/婆婆 (together 公婆; his family is her 婆家); a husband's in-laws are 岳父/岳母, colloquially 丈人 (老丈人) and 丈母娘 (her parents' home is the 岳家; for her it is her 娘家). Face to face, after 改口, both say 爸/妈.
rules.why: CC-CEDICT: 公婆 'husband's parents; parents-in-law', 婆家 'husband's family (traditionally where the wife moves into)', 岳父 'wife's father', 岳母 'wife's mother', 丈人 'wife's father', 老丈人 '(coll.) father-in-law (wife's father)', 丈母娘 'wife's mother', 岳家 'wife's parents' home', 娘家 'wife's family (before marriage)'; Xinhua 娘家: '已婚女子称自己父母的家'. CC-CEDICT 改口: a bride 'starts to call her husband's parents 爸爸 and 妈妈'; 改口费 goes to both the new daughter-in-law and the new son-in-law.

rules.rule: The -子 words for a spouse's siblings — 大伯子, 小叔子, 大姑子, 小姑子 (husband's) and 大舅子, 小舅子, 大姨子, 小姨子 (wife's) — are colloquial words for talking about them, not titles to call them by. Face to face, follow your partner: their older siblings are 哥/姐 (or 大哥, 二姐…) to you, and younger ones are called by name.
rules.why: CC-CEDICT tags them '(coll.)' and states it explicitly for 小姨子: '(term not used to directly address her)'; 现代汉语词典 labels them 〈口〉 (all but 小舅子) and defines them only as relationships (e.g. 小叔子 '丈夫的弟弟'); Xinhua: 大姑子 '多用于口语'. A guest post for Western women married to Chinese men (Speaking of China) advises simply following your husband's terms for his relatives.

rules.rule: Once you are married, call your partner's relatives what your partner calls them (随配偶称呼): the parents 爸/妈; the grandparents 爷爷/奶奶 or 外公/外婆; uncles and aunts 伯伯, 叔叔, 姑姑, 舅舅, 姨… and their spouses; your partner's older siblings 哥/姐 and their spouses 嫂子/姐夫; younger siblings by name, as your partner does. The in-law words (公公, 婆婆, 岳父, 大伯子, 小姨子…) are for talking about them.
rules.why: CC-CEDICT 改口: a bride 'starts to call her husband's parents 爸爸 and 妈妈'. A guest post on Speaking of China, written for Western women married to Chinese men, says that besides 公公/婆婆 'in many cases, people just use the same words as their husband use, which are 爸 or 妈', and that with the older generation 'just to follow your husband is fine'; ETtoday (2026-05-17) reports that following one's spouse in calling the in-laws 爸爸/媽媽 after marriage is still widespread. CC-CEDICT 小姨子: '(term not used to directly address her)'.
rules.regional_note: Another custom names some in-laws from your children's point of view (Xinhua 叔叔 ②: '丈夫的弟弟' — a wife calling her husband's younger brother 叔叔). Local habits differ: check with your partner.
